title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1LC0RD_0LA0RB_0LE1LF_1RF0LC_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1LC0RD_0LA0RB_0LE1LF_1RF0LC_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Its tape is a prefix of blocks 1^2 0 at the left end followed by a long word of the tokens 1 0, 1^2 0 and 0^3 1. The left end moves out three cells at a time, at irregular moments roughly 1.5 times apart; no counter, no fixed rule for the word, and no restructure rule has been found.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1011 steps.

What it does. Every time the left end moves, the tape reads C>0 0^2 1 0 (1^2 0)^m V with V a word of the tokens 1 0, 1^2 0, 0^3 1. The prefix length m goes up and down (16 to 18 in the last ten extensions). The left end moved at steps 3.2·109, 8.1·109, 2.3·1010, 3.6·1010, 4.3·1010, 6.5·1010: the gaps do not double, so this is not a plain counter.

Why it is hard. No macro structure has been found: no closed tape language from short windows was found, the word V changes everywhere between extensions, and the extension times follow no visible rule.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1011 steps without a halt; 262 cells visited (203 left of the start, 59 right), 115 ones at the end.

claims.title: The left end grows three cells at a time
claims.text: All 61 moments in the first 1011 steps when the head, in state C, reaches a new cell at the left end have the shape C>0 0^2 1 0 (1^2 0)^m V, with V made of 1 0, 1^2 0 and 0^3 1; each is followed within 12 steps by two more new cells. m is not monotone: it fell 14 times, the last time at step 35,830,421,385 (from 18 to 16).

claims.title: Irregular, roughly geometric growth
claims.text: The left end moved at steps 1.5·10<sup>9</sup>, 3.2·10<sup>9</sup>, 8.1·10<sup>9</sup>, 2.3·10<sup>10</sup>, 3.6·10<sup>10</sup>, 4.3·10<sup>10</sup> and 6.5·10<sup>10</sup>; the ratios range from 1.2 to 2.8. The width grows like the logarithm of the step count (236 cells at 10<sup>9</sup> steps, 262 at 10<sup>11</sup>).

claims.title: The structure, and the question itself
claims.text: Not known: what the word V encodes, what decides when the left end moves, and whether the machine halts (it halts only in state F reading a 1).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>11</sup> steps without stopping. Its tape is a long word of three tokens that grows at the left end three cells at a time, at irregular moments; no rule behind it has been found. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 262 cells visited.
The left end grows three cells at a time, 61 times so far.
Irregular ratios between the times of successive extensions.

sections.heading: A word with no visible rule
html:
Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the left end of the tape. It is then always in state C, and the tape reads C>0 0^2 1 0 (1^2 0)^m V: a run of m blocks 1^2 0, and then a long word V built from the three tokens 1 0, 1^2 0 and 0^3 1. Within twelve steps the head moves out two more cells and goes back right; three cells are added each time.

Unlike the counters of its neighbours in this group, the prefix does not simply grow: m went up and down 14 times in the first 1011 steps, and V changes along its whole length between extensions. The moments of the last seven extensions are 1.5, 3.2, 8.1, 23, 36, 43 and 65 billion steps. Their ratios range from 1.2 to 2.8, so this is not a binary counter.

sections.heading: What is missing
html: No macro rule is known. A closed tape language from windows of up to 6 cells (and of 8 cells read from the other side) does not close, so not even the place of a possible halt (state F reading a 1) is pinned down. The next step is to find out what V encodes, for example by testing whether the tokens are digits in some base and the extensions are carries.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.053). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 236 cells (179 left of the start, 53 right), with a density of 1s of 0.436.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: irregular word with a slowly growing left prefix (structure not found)
summary: Open. No halt in 10^11 steps; the tape grows on the left three cells at a time, at irregular times, and the word in the middle shows no rule found so far.
